newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end lower after slightly overpriced auction.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end lower after slightly overpriced auction.

text.p: Key March 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures failed to keep Monday's momentum and closed lower on Tuesday as the new 10-year bonds auctioned earlier in the day were slightly overpriced, traders said.
The auction produced a lowest price of 100.80 and an average price of 100.84. The lowest price was higher than some bidders had expected, traders said.
This slightly curbed investors' appetite for the bonds, which carried a record low 2.6 percent coupon, they said.
The March closed at 126.45, down 0.25 from the previous finish. On Monday, the contract hit a record high of 126.83.
The contract rosed as high as 126.77 in the morning, but its rise was dampened by hedge sales starting in the afternoon, traders said. A total of 38,265 contracts changed hands.

"At first, it looked a fairly good auction," said a dealer at a Japanese securities house. "But brokers lowered offer prices for the new bonds soon after the auction results were announced. This suggested sales of the bonds were not as aggressive as we had expected."
The amounts taken by a big-four brokerage house and a city bank's securities unit amounted to more than 40 percent of total bids, traders said.
The yield of the key 182nd 10-year JGB closed at a day high of 2.380 percent, up from Monday's 2.350. It jumped in late trade as the dollar hit a new 47-month high of 123.30 yen.
Earlier in the day, some buying of four-year and six-year cash JGBs was detected. The buyers were probably tapping into relatively cheap parts of the yield curve, traders said.
But some said a downside price risk may emerge if the U.S. fourth-quarter employment cost index due at 1330 GMT improves.
"If U.S. interest rates start to rise after the data, that could easily drive other nations' rates higher," a dealer at a major brokerage said. -- Tokyo Treasury +81-3-3432-8570
